subject: SignalHub — Prompt observability integration & pilot
messages:
From: Samir Patel <samir@signalhub.ai>
To: rishi_malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Cc: Denise Kline <denise.k@consultrix.com>
Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: SignalHub + Redwood — prompt observability proposal

Hi Rishi,

Great to meet you at the summit last month — following up on our conversation about adding SignalHub's prompt observability hooks into Redwood's SDK surface. We put together a short proposal (attached) and a sample telemetry schema for prompt-level events. High level:

- Lightweight SDK shim (LangChain/LlamaIndex compatibility) that emits anonymized prompt hashes, latency, tokens-in/out, and a trace_id for chaining with existing traces.
- Optional server-side ingestion endpoint for teams that want a managed SignalHub pipeline (SaaS) vs. self-hosted forwarder.
- Pilot scope: 6 weeks, 2 canonical workloads (chat + batch embed indexing) to validate cost/latency impact and quality correlation signals.

Attachments: signalhub-integration-proposal.pdf, sample_prompt_telemetry_schema.json

Would Redwood be open to running a short technical pilot? Denise from Consultrix (cc'd) will support security/compliance and procurement discussions.

Thanks,
Samir Patel
Head of Partnerships | SignalHub
samir@signalhub.ai
+1 (415) 555-0198

From: rishi_malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir@signalhub.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SignalHub + Redwood — prompt observability proposal

Samir — thanks for the note and the materials. This is aligned with a few asks we've been getting from ISVs: better prompt-level hooks, consistent trace correlation, and a low-risk path for customers to opt into telemetry. We are interested in a pilot but need to clarify a few technical and commercial points first.

Quick asks from our side:
- Can you confirm that the telemetry payloads can be configured to strip PII and only emit prompt hashes and token metadata? Our default requirement is zero raw prompt text leaving customer-controlled compute.
- For the LangChain/LlamaIndex shims: do you provide a Python package and a JS shim? We typically run both in hosted and Dedicated stacks.
- Performance: do you have microbenchmarks for prefix caching scenarios — e.g., adding the shim should not increase median token latency by >5% for <1k prompt length.
- Security: Denise, can you share the SOC2/ISO references and a standard NDA/DPAs you prefer? We'll loop in our security team if needed.

I'm looping in Karthik (cc) to scope the runtime changes and Marissa to cover pilot commercial terms. If we all agree, we can aim to start an integration sprint the week of 7/12.

Best,
Rishi Malhotra
Director, Platform Partnerships | Redwood Inference
rishi@redwood.com

Thanks Samir — I dug into the sample schema and proposal. A few technical notes and a suggested minimal implementation plan below.

Summary of what I tested:
- Quick bench: adding a local shim that emits non-blocking JSON over UDP to a collector had ~1.2% median token latency impact on a 512-token chat workload (local dev machine).
- Hashing approach: we prefer salted SHA256 hashes (customer-specified salt) so we never store raw prompts even for dedup. SignalHub's schema seems compatible but we need an explicit config flag for salt management.

Proposed minimal pilot implementation (3 sprints, ~6 weeks):
- Sprint 0 (prep, 1 week): finalize PII/telemetry schema, NDA, and provide a small sample dataset (sanitized).
- Sprint 1 (runtime shim, 2 weeks): deliver Python shim for LangChain and a lightweight JS shim for Redwood's edge SDK. Include a toggle to emit events async and a fallback no-op implementation.
- Sprint 2 (ingest + dashboard, 2 weeks): deploy SignalHub collector in our staging VPC (managed forwarder) and seed dashboards for token-level histograms and prompt-quality correlation.
- Sprint 3 (validation & docs, 1 week): run 2 canonical workloads (chat bot + embedding re-index) and produce an evaluation report with cost/latency delta.

Open technical questions for SignalHub:
1) Retention & access control: default retention in your managed ingestion and how RBAC is enforced.
2) Forwarder options: we can accept a signed webhook or a Kafka sink — which do you prefer?
3) Tracing correlation: you mentioned a trace_id. We need 1:1 mapping between Redwood request IDs and SignalHub trace ids for sampling analysis.

Samir — can you answer the three bullets above? If this looks good we can spin up a shared Drive folder and a HubSpot opportunity and draft an MoU.

-karthik
Senior Engineer, Runtime Integrations | Redwood Inference

Samir / Denise — thanks for the patience while we scoped this internally. From a commercial/pilot perspective we're supportive and can agree to the 6-week pilot outlined by Karthik with the following mutual action plan (MAP):

Mutual Action Plan (MAP):
- 7/12: Project kickoff (intro + security checklist) — Redwood: Rishi, Karthik, Chloe. SignalHub: Samir, eng lead.
- 7/12 - 7/16: Sprint 0 (NDA & sanitized dataset transfer).
- 7/19 - 7/30: Sprint 1 (runtime shim delivery).
- 8/02 - 8/13: Sprint 2 (ingest + dashboard in staging).
- 8/16 - 8/20: Sprint 3 (validation & formal report).

Commercial notes:
- Pilot is non-billable for basic integration (up to 6 engineer-weeks shared). Any additional managed ingestion beyond a single staging forwarder will be charged at SignalHub's standard pilot rate; please provide a short addendum if needed.
- Data handling: Redwood requires opt-in from customers for any telemetry. SignalHub must support the salted-hash model and provide DPA language in your standard contract.

Next steps: Samir — can you confirm acceptance of the MAP and provide your preferred NDA template. I'll create the HubSpot opportunity and the Drive folder (link below). Suggested demo window for kickoff: 7/12 10–11am PT.
